1. Khuddānukhuddakapañha 1. Question on the Lesser and Minor Rules

“Bhante nāgasena, bhāsitampetaṁ bhagavatā—“Venerable Nāgasena, the Blessed One said: ‘abhiññāyāhaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammaṁ desemi no anabhiññāyā’ti. ‘Bhikkhus, I teach the Dhamma having directly known it, not without direct knowledge.’ Puna ca vinayapaññattiyā evaṁ bhaṇitaṁ—But in the Vinaya regulations he also said: ‘ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, saṅgho mamaccayena khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhanatū’ti. ‘Ānanda, if the Saṅgha wishes, after my passing it may abolish the lesser and minor training rules.’ Kiṁ nu kho, bhante nāgasena, khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni duppaññattāni, udāhu avatthusmiṁ ajānitvā paññattāni, yaṁ bhagavā attano accayena khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhanāpeti? Venerable Nāgasena, were the lesser and minor rules badly laid down? Or were they laid down without a proper basis, through ignorance, so that the Blessed One has them abolished after his passing? Yadi, bhante nāgasena, bhagavatā bhaṇitaṁ—If, Venerable Nāgasena, the Blessed One said ‘abhiññāyāhaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammaṁ desemi no anabhiññāyā’ti, tena hi ‘ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, saṅgho mamaccayena khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhanatū’ti yaṁ vacanaṁ, taṁ micchā. ‘I teach the Dhamma having directly known it, not without direct knowledge,’ then the statement ‘Ānanda, if the Saṅgha wishes, after my passing it may abolish the lesser and minor rules’ is false. Yadi tathāgatena vinayapaññattiyā evaṁ bhaṇitaṁ—And if the Tathāgata said that in the Vinaya regulations, ‘ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, saṅgho mamaccayena khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhanatū’ti tena hi ‘abhiññāyāhaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammaṁ desemi no anabhiññāyā’ti tampi vacanaṁ micchā. ‘Ānanda, if the Saṅgha wishes, after my passing it may abolish the lesser and minor rules’, then the statement ‘I teach the Dhamma having directly known it’ is also false. Ayampi ubhato koṭiko pañho sukhumo nipuṇo gambhīro sugambhīro dunnijjhāpayo, so tavānuppatto, tattha te ñāṇabalavipphāraṁ dassehī”ti. This question is two-horned, subtle, refined, profound, very profound, and hard to make others understand. It has come to you; show here the power and reach of your wisdom.”

“Bhāsitampetaṁ, mahārāja, bhagavatā ‘abhiññāyāhaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammaṁ desemi no anabhiññāyā’ti, vinayapaññattiyāpi evaṁ bhaṇitaṁ—“Your majesty, the Blessed One did say ‘Bhikkhus, I teach the Dhamma having directly known it, not without direct knowledge,’ and he also said in the Vinaya regulations: ‘ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, saṅgho mamaccayena khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhanatū’ti, taṁ pana, mahārāja, tathāgato bhikkhū vīmaṁsamāno āha—‘Ānanda, if the Saṅgha wishes, after my passing it may abolish the lesser and minor rules.’ But the Tathāgata said this as a way of testing the bhikkhus, thinking: ‘ukkalessanti nu kho mama sāvakā mayā vissajjāpīyamānā mamaccayena khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni, udāhu ādiyissantī’ti. ‘When I let them go, will my disciples, after my passing, cast off the lesser and minor rules, or will they take them up?’

Yathā, mahārāja, cakkavattī rājā putte evaṁ vadeyya ‘ayaṁ kho, tātā, mahājanapado sabbadisāsu sāgarapariyanto, dukkaro, tātā, tāvatakena balena dhāretuṁ, etha tumhe, tātā, mamaccayena paccante paccante dese pajahathā’ti. Just as, your majesty, a wheel-turning monarch might say to his sons: ‘My sons, this great realm reaches to the ocean in every direction. It is hard, my sons, to hold it with so little strength. After my passing, give up the border regions, one by one.’ Api nu kho te, mahārāja, kumārā pituaccayena hatthagate janapade sabbe te paccante paccante dese muñceyyun”ti? Now, your majesty, would those princes, after their father’s death, release all the border regions of the realm that had come into their hands?” “Na hi, bhante, rājato, bhante, luddhatarā kumārā rajjalobhena taduttariṁ diguṇatiguṇaṁ janapadaṁ pariggaṇheyyuṁ, kiṁ pana te hatthagataṁ janapadaṁ muñceyyun”ti? Certainly not, Venerable Sir. Princes are greedier than their king; out of greed for sovereignty they would seize a realm twice or three times larger. How could they let go of the realm already in their hands?” “Evameva kho, mahārāja, tathāgato bhikkhū vīmaṁsamāno evamāha—“In just the same way, your majesty, the Tathāgata, testing the bhikkhus, said: ‘ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, saṅgho mamaccayena khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhanatū’ti. ‘Ānanda, if the Saṅgha wishes, after my passing it may abolish the lesser and minor rules.’ Dukkhaparimuttiyā, mahārāja, buddhaputtā dhammalobhena aññampi uttariṁ diyaḍḍhasikkhāpadasataṁ gopeyyuṁ, kiṁ pana pakatipaññattaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ muñceyyun”ti? Out of a desire for release from suffering, your majesty, the Buddha’s sons, with a greed for the Dhamma, would guard even another hundred and fifty rules beyond these. How then would they let go of the rules laid down in the ordinary way?”

“Bhante nāgasena, yaṁ bhagavā āha—“Venerable Nāgasena, regarding what the Blessed One called ‘khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī’ti, etthāyaṁ jano sammūḷho vimatijāto adhikato saṁsayapakkhando. ‘lesser and minor rules,’ people here are confused, doubtful, perplexed, and caught in uncertainty. Katamāni tāni khuddakāni sikkhāpadāni, katamāni anukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī”ti? Which are the lesser rules, and which are the minor rules?” “Dukkaṭaṁ, mahārāja, khuddakaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ, dubbhāsitaṁ anukhuddakaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ, imāni dve khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni, pubbakehipi, mahārāja, mahātherehi ettha vimati uppāditā, tehipi ekajjhaṁ na kato dhammasaṇṭhitipariyāye bhagavatā eso pañho upadiṭṭho”ti. “A wrongdoing (dukkaṭa), your majesty, is a lesser rule; a misspeaking (dubbhāsita) is a minor rule. These two are the ‘lesser and minor rules.’ Even the great elders of former times, your majesty, fell into doubt over this, and they did not reach agreement on it. The Blessed One explained this matter in the discourse on the establishment of the Dhamma.” “Ciranikkhittaṁ, bhante nāgasena, jinarahassaṁ ajjetarahi loke vivaṭaṁ pākaṭaṁ katan”ti. “Venerable Nāgasena, a secret of the Conqueror long concealed has today been opened and made plain in the world.”

Khuddānukhuddakapañho paṭhamo. Question on the Lesser and Minor Rules first
